title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by attackers to conduct post-exploitation activities against Thailand's Ministry of Finance, operating in an unattended mode that bypassed approval prompts for dangerous commands. The system was used to automate attack tasks across a compromised network, including creating malware, staging exploit code, and accessing multiple systems through stolen credentials and web shells. This shows a failure mode where an AI system was operated without human oversight during active malicious use.

The deployment occurred within a network already breached by attackers who had gained initial access to ministry systems. Detection happened through exposed directories on a remote server containing attack artifacts and stolen files, discovered by security researchers. A system designed to operate autonomously without human approval proved effective at scale for the attacker's purposes, operating undetected for a period of days before authorities were notified.

It is not established whether the Hermes agent was purpose-built for this attack, what specific vulnerabilities enabled the initial compromise, or what technical measures the ministry had in place to detect or prevent such autonomous activity.

summary:
# Summary

Thai cybersecurity researchers discovered that attackers used an autonomous AI agent called Hermes to target Thailand's Ministry of Finance starting in mid to late June 2026. Between July 9 and 13, three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server contained 585 files totaling 470 megabytes of attack code and stolen credentials. The operator deployed a custom malware implant named Hades across Windows and Linux systems, created custom exploitation tools targeting the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure and GlassFish servers, and successfully accessed multiple systems within the ministry's network through compromised session cookies and web shells.

The attack was largely automated through Hermes running in unattended YOLO mode, which bypasses approval prompts for dangerous commands. Evidence indicates the operator was Chinese-speaking and possessed detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network topology. Researchers identified four servers linked to the operation and staged exploit code for multiple known vulnerabilities. Thailand's national cybersecurity authorities received notification on July 15, 2026, and acknowledged the report the same day. The research was conducted jointly by security firm Hunt.io and independent researcher Bob Diachenko.
